evidence: Cic. Amic. 2: domī in hēmicycliō sedentem
terms.comment: The state of sitting. Sitting down is cōnsīdō, though the imperative sedē also serves for “sit down” (Mart. 8.67.6).

terms.gloss: sit down, take a seat; settle
evidence: Ov. Met. 13.930–931: in illō caespite cōnsēdī
Liv. 7.26.3: corvus repente in galeā cōnsēdit
terms.comment: The act of sitting down, also of a bird landing. “Sit down!” is Cōnsīde!

phrases.latin: sedēbāmus ergō in puppī simul ūniversī et lūcentia sīdera cōnsīderābāmus
phrases.english: so we were all sitting together on the stern, gazing at the shining stars

phrases.latin: curre, age, et inlōtōs revocā, Calliste, ministrōs; sternantur lectī: Caeciliāne, sedē
phrases.english: Quick, Callistus, run and call the waiters back, unwashed as they are; have the couches spread: Caecilianus, do sit down

phrases.latin: ego prīmus in illō caespite cōnsēdī, dum līna madentia siccō
phrases.english: I was the first to sit down on that turf, while I dried my wet lines

sources: Lewis & Short: sedeo · Lewis & Short: consido
